conservative.read: This plan aims for capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration risk, holding a larger cash buffer for stability. Drawdowns should be minimal.

moves.note: Add quality name with good risk/reward

Trim SPY to 25% to address concentration and increase cash.

balanced.read: This balanced approach targets around 2.5% monthly return by reducing leverage and concentration while adding quality names. It aims for risk-first growth, with a moderate cash buffer and controlled exposure to both broad markets and specific tech sectors. Drawdowns are expected to be manageable.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and free up capital.
Increase leveraged ETFs SOXL and SPAL to 6% each.
Add SMH to 19% and CRWD to 15% to concentrate on strong performers.
Buy AMAT at 8% as a new high-conviction semiconductor play.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% monthly return by increasing leverage and concentrating on the strongest scanner setups, including leveraged ETFs. It carries significantly higher risk, with the potential for larger gains and much larger drawdowns, amplified by leverage and daily rebalancing of leveraged ETFs. A smaller cash buffer means less cushion in downturns.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and increase cash.
Maximize QQQI to 30% and add QQQ to 20% for steady income and stability.
Sell CRWD and SMH to zero to remove high-beta and sector concentration.
This plan prioritizes generating consistent monthly distributions.

income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% monthly return through distributions from income-oriented ETFs and broad market exposure. It minimizes volatility and risk by cutting leverage and high-beta single names, holding a significant cash buffer. While distributions are prioritized, NAV can still decline in market selloffs.
